subject: Numeracy
title: Counting beyond 10
objectives: Children will say numbers to 15 in order.
Children will count groups of up to 15 objects.
content: Saying numbers 11 to 15, counting groups of 11 to 15, and counting in twos.
teachingActivities: Use a ten frame or two rows of five to show that eleven is ten and one more; say teen numbers slowly; count out groups of 11 to 15 in tens and ones with ten frames; count in twos with pairs such as shoes and gloves.
learnerActivities: Say numbers to 15 in order, count groups of up to 15 objects and count in twos.
assessment: Observe whether each child says numbers to 15 and counts groups beyond 10.

lessons.title: Saying 11 to 15
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say the numbers 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 in order.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10 and say one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Walk along a number line saying "nine, ten, eleven, twelve."
teacherActivities: Say the new numbers slowly with the drum beat.
Show numeral cards 11 to 15 and say each name.
Walk along the number line from 10 to 15.
learnerActivities: Children say them with the beat.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say the new numbers slowly with the drum beat. Children: Children say them with the beat.
Step 2. Teacher: Show numeral cards 11 to 15 and say each name. Children: Children repeat each name.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk along the number line from 10 to 15. Children: Children walk and count.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What comes after twelve?" Children: Child says thirteen.

practical.title: Walk to fifteen
practical.safety: Keep the number line flat and secured. Walk slowly and one at a time.

differentiation.support: Count from nine to thirteen only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count to twenty.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Count from one to fifteen together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count up to fifteen steps with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say the numbers 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Ten and some more
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show numbers 11 to 15 as ten and some more on a ten frame.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10 and say one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show a full ten frame and say "This is ten. Eleven is ten and one more."
teacherActivities: Fill a ten frame and put one counter beside it.
Add one more and say twelve.
Let children make 11 to 15 on a ten frame and extras.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Fill a ten frame and put one counter beside it. Children: Children count eleven.
Step 2. Teacher: Add one more and say twelve. Children: Children count twelve.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children make 11 to 15 on a ten frame and extras. Children: Child fills and adds counters.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many in all?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Ten frame numbers
practical.safety: Use large flat counters and supervise placing. Keep ten frames on a mat.

differentiation.support: Fill the ten frame together and add up to three.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a number beyond fifteen.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many in the ten frame?

expectedOutcomes: Shows numbers 11 to 15 on a ten frame
lessons.conclusion: Put the frames away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Count out ten and then a few more objects.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show numbers 11 to 15 as ten and some more on a ten frame" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A full ten frame with extras

lessons.title: Counting groups to fifteen
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count groups of 11 to 15 objects.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10 and say one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show a basket and say "How many are in this basket? Let us count carefully."
teacherActivities: Count a group of twelve moving each into a tray.
Say how many and show the numeral.
Give each pair a basket to count.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count a group of twelve moving each into a tray. Children: Children count aloud.
Step 2. Teacher: Say how many and show the numeral. Children: Children say twelve.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each pair a basket to count. Children: Pairs count and agree.
Step 4. Teacher: Match baskets to numeral cards. Children: Child matches a card.

practical.title: Count the basket
steps: Move each object as you count.
practical.safety: Use large safe objects only and supervise closely. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Use a basket of eleven or twelve and count in two steps.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count a group of twenty.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How did you not lose count?

lessons.conclusion: Put the baskets away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Count up to fifteen objects at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count groups of 11 to 15 objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting in twos
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count pairs of objects in twos.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10 and say one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show a pair of shoes and say "One pair is two shoes. Two pairs are four shoes."
teacherActivities: Put shoes in pairs and count in twos.
Use gloves or cups to count in twos.
Let children make pairs and count them.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put shoes in pairs and count in twos. Children: Children count two, four, six.
Step 2. Teacher: Use gloves or cups to count in twos. Children: Children count with the teacher.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children make pairs and count them. Children: Child makes pairs and counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Two, four, six, eight, ten." Children: Children chant in twos.

practical.title: Count the pairs
practical.safety: Use clean shoes and wash hands after. Keep walkways clear.

differentiation.support: Count two pairs first and say the numbers together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count to twenty in twos.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many shoes in two pairs?
What comes after six in twos?

lessons.conclusion: Put the pairs away and count in twos.
lessons.homeConnection: Count socks and shoes in twos at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count pairs of objects in twos" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 counting beyond ten check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child counts beyond ten.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10 and say one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: number line, ten frame and counting baskets.
At each station ask "How many?" and watch.
Record each child’s level and highest number counted.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: number line, ten frame and counting baskets. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many?" and watch. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and highest number counted. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Beyond ten stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large counters. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and count to twelve.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count to thirty.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says numbers to 15; counts groups beyond 10; uses a ten frame; counts in twos.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep counting beyond ten at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child counts beyond ten" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
